name: Donald Knuth
milestone_by_age_26: TAOCP Volume 1 was published in 1968 at age 30; while Knuth signed the Addison-Wesley contract in January 1962 (age 24) and completed his PhD in June 1963 (age 25), no seminal publication or major product shipped by age 26. His early papers (e.g. 'An imaginary number system,' 1960) were notable but not seminal in the way TAOCP would become.
early_history_summary: Knuth graduated from Case Institute of Technology in 1960 with a simultaneous BS and MS, then earned his PhD from Caltech in 1963. He was a consultant for Burroughs Corporation and signed a book contract with Addison-Wesley in 1962, but the first volume of TAOCP was not published until 1968.
family_context_summary: Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to Ervin Henry Knuth, a teacher at a Lutheran high school and church organist, and Louise Marie Bohning. He describes his heritage as Midwestern Lutheran German.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a teacher and church organist; no specific technical or mathematical domain expertise documented in the family.
evidence_summary: Knuth's seminal work, The Art of Computer Programming, was published in 1968 when he was 30. While he had notable early achievements including a simultaneous BS/MS from Case, a PhD from Caltech, and published papers before age 26, none constitute a material milestone as defined by the rubric (seminal publication, notable product, or significant discovery). The TAOCP contract was signed at 24 but the book did not ship until age 30.

name: Reed Hastings
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Pure Software in October 1991 at age 31 and Netflix in 1997 at age 37; by age 26 (c.1986), Hastings was serving in the Peace Corps in Swaziland with no tech milestone.
early_history_summary: Hastings served in the Peace Corps in Swaziland from 1983 to 1986, then worked as a software developer at Adaptive Technology from around 1988 to 1991. He founded Pure Software in October 1991 at age 31, which went public in 1995 and was acquired by Rational Software in 1997. He co-founded Netflix later that year.
evidence_summary: Hastings' first company, Pure Software, was founded in 1991 when he was 31. By age 26, he was in the Peace Corps in Swaziland with no tech industry involvement. His tech career began around 1988 at Adaptive Technology, well after age 26.

name: Reid Hoffman
milestone_by_age_26: Founded SocialNet in 1997 at age 30 and LinkedIn in 2002 at age 35; by age 26 (c.1993), Hoffman was studying philosophy at Oxford as a Marshall Scholar with no tech milestone.
early_history_summary: Hoffman earned degrees in symbolic systems from Stanford and philosophy from Oxford as a Marshall Scholar. He joined Apple Computer in 1994 at age 27, later worked at Fujitsu, and founded his first company SocialNet in 1997 at age 30. He joined PayPal as COO in 2000 and co-founded LinkedIn in 2002.
evidence_summary: Hoffman's first entrepreneurial venture, SocialNet, was founded in 1997 when he was 30. By age 26, he was studying philosophy at Oxford. His tech career began at Apple in 1994 at age 27, after leaving academia. No material tech milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Evan You
milestone_by_age_26: Released Vue.js, a lightweight JavaScript frontend framework, publicly on GitHub and Hacker News in February 2014 at age 26, attracting immediate community adoption and growing into one of the top three frontend frameworks globally.
early_history_summary: You was born in Wuxi, China, and received early access to computers through his father, who bought him a 486 computer in primary school. He initially pursued design rather than engineering, studying at Colgate University and later Parsons School of Design. While working at Google Creative Lab with AngularJS, he created Vue.js as a side project to extract the lightweight features he liked from Angular, committing the first code in July 2013 and releasing it publicly in February 2014.
family_context_summary: Born in Wuxi, China, to a family that valued education. His father bought him a 486 computer during primary school and encouraged him to study abroad, fulfilling the father's unaccomplished dream of studying abroad.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father encouraged study abroad but no specific tech domain expertise documented in the family. The family was middle-class and education-oriented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early computer access, design background, Google experience, AngularJS, self-taught, Hacker News distribution
evidence_summary: You created Vue.js as a side project while working at Google Creative Lab, releasing it publicly on GitHub and Hacker News in February 2014 at age 26. He had early access to computers through his father, who bought him a 486 computer in primary school, but initially pursued design rather than engineering. His experience with AngularJS at Google inspired him to create a lighter alternative. Vue.js quickly gained traction, reaching the Hacker News front page and growing into one of the top three frontend frameworks globally. Note: one source lists birth year as 1989, but the CSV and another interview source indicate 1987; either way, the first public release was at or before age 26.

name: Dan Abramov
milestone_by_age_26: Released Redux, a JavaScript state management library, in June 2015 at age 22, which quickly became the dominant state management solution in the React ecosystem with billions of npm downloads.
early_history_summary: Abramov was born in Omsk, Russia, and started coding around age twelve, learning JavaScript at fourteen when his step-father asked him to build a database to track photoshoot information. He was largely self-taught, finishing high school in 2009 and briefly attending university before dropping out to work at DataArt. He later worked at Stampsy, where he adopted React in 2014. He created Redux in 2015 while preparing a conference talk for React Europe, demonstrating hot reloading and time-travel debugging. The CSV lists birth_year as 1984, but multiple sources indicate he was born on September 4, 1992, which is consistent with his high school graduation in 2009 and his description as a 22-year-old at React Europe 2015.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Omsk, Russia. Started coding around age twelve, self-taught through online resources. No significant financial resources or family connections in tech documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Step-father requested him to develop a database to track photoshoot information, which led to learning JavaScript at age fourteen. No specific tech domain expertise in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, early coding, JavaScript, React ecosystem, online community, Russian outsider, curiosity-driven
evidence_summary: Abramov, a self-taught developer from Omsk, Russia, created Redux in 2015 at age 22 while preparing a conference talk for React Europe on hot reloading and time-travel debugging. He started coding around age twelve and learned JavaScript at fourteen when his step-father asked him to build a database. Redux quickly became the dominant state management library in the React ecosystem. He joined Facebook's React Core team later in 2015. His path was driven by curiosity and online learning rather than formal education or family connections. Note: the CSV lists birth_year as 1984, but multiple sources indicate 1992, consistent with his high school graduation in 2009 and his being described as 22 at React Europe 2015.

name: Bram Cohen
milestone_by_age_26: Released the first BitTorrent client and protocol implementation on July 2, 2001 at age 25, creating what would become one of the most widely used peer-to-peer file-sharing protocols, accounting for 43-70% of all internet traffic by 2009.
early_history_summary: Cohen grew up on the Upper West Side of Manhattan as the son of a teacher and computer scientist. He learned BASIC programming at age five on a family Timex Sinclair computer. He attended Stuyvesant High School, passed the AIME, and graduated in 1993. He attended SUNY Buffalo but dropped out to work for dot-com companies, including MojoNation, whose distributed file architecture inspired BitTorrent. He designed the BitTorrent protocol in April 2001 and released the first implementation on July 2, 2001.
family_context_summary: Grew up on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, New York City, as the son of a teacher and computer scientist. Had access to a Timex Sinclair computer at home from age five.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a computer scientist, which provided early access to computers and programming. Mother was a teacher.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early programming, self-taught, Stuyvesant, dot-com experience, P2P community, computer scientist father, Timex Sinclair
evidence_summary: Cohen learned to program at age five on a family Timex Sinclair computer, influenced by his computer scientist father. He attended the prestigious Stuyvesant High School and passed the AIME before dropping out of SUNY Buffalo to work at dot-com companies. At age 25, he released the first BitTorrent client in July 2001, creating what would become one of the most widely used P2P protocols. His experience at MojoNation provided the technical inspiration for BitTorrent's distributed download architecture. He co-founded CodeCon and was active in the San Francisco Bay Area P2P-hackers community.

name: John von Neumann
milestone_by_age_26: Published 'Eine Axiomatisierung der Mengenlehre' in 1925 at age 21, a seminal axiomatization of set theory introducing the framework now known as NBG (von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel) set theory, and published the definition of ordinal numbers (still used today) at age 20 in 1923.
early_history_summary: Von Neumann was born in Budapest to a wealthy Jewish banking family and was recognized as a child prodigy, receiving private tutoring in multiple languages and advanced mathematics from age 15 under Gábor Szegő. He studied at the University of Berlin, ETH Zurich, and the University of Budapest, simultaneously pursuing chemistry and mathematics. He published his first mathematics paper with Fekete in 1922, the definition of ordinal numbers at age 20, and his seminal axiomatization of set theory in 1925. He earned his PhD in 1926 and studied under Hilbert at Göttingen.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy, non-observant Jewish family in Budapest. His father, Max von Neumann, was a banker with a doctorate in law who was elevated to Hungarian nobility in 1913. The family lived in an 18-room apartment above the Kann-Heller offices. Three generations of the Kann family lived in the same building.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a banker with a doctorate in law, elevated to Hungarian nobility for service to the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Mother came from the well-to-do Kann family. No specific mathematical domain expertise, but highly educated and wealthy with strong emphasis on education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, private tutors, elite education, child prodigy, Budapest mathematical tradition, Hilbert, Göttingen, nobility
evidence_summary: Von Neumann was born into a wealthy Jewish banking family in Budapest and was recognized as a child prodigy, receiving private tutoring in multiple languages and advanced mathematics from age 15 under Gábor Szegő. By age 21, he had published his seminal axiomatization of set theory (1925), introducing the framework now known as NBG set theory, and had published the definition of ordinal numbers at age 20. His father's wealth and nobility status provided exceptional educational opportunities, including study at the University of Berlin, ETH Zurich, and under Hilbert at Göttingen. He was tutored by governesses in English, French, German, and Italian from a young age.

name: Kiichiro Toyoda
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Toyota Motor Co. in 1937 at age 43; by age 26 (c.1920), Toyoda had just graduated from university and was working in the family loom business (Toyoda Boshoku) with no material milestone such as founding a company or making a significant discovery.
early_history_summary: Toyoda was born in 1894 as the eldest son of Sakichi Toyoda, a prolific inventor of textile machinery. He grew up around factories and machines, graduated from university in July 1920, and returned to work at the family business Toyoda Boshoku. He later developed the Type G Automatic Loom in the 1920s and established the Automotive Production Division within Toyoda Automatic Loom Works in 1933, eventually founding Toyota Motor Co. in 1937.
family_context_summary: Born as the eldest son of Sakichi Toyoda, a prolific inventor of textile machinery. Grew up in company housing on factory premises, surrounded by people designing, creating, and fixing machines from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Sakichi Toyoda was a prolific inventor of textile machinery (looms), providing direct domain exposure to engineering and manufacturing from childhood. Kiichiro grew up seeing machines designed and built around him.
evidence_summary: Toyoda founded Toyota Motor Co. in 1937 at age 43. By age 26 (June 1920), he had just graduated from university and was working in the family loom business (Toyoda Boshoku), learning spinning technology on the shop floor. While he came from a prominent inventing family (his father Sakichi Toyoda was a prolific loom inventor), no material milestone such as a company founding, significant invention, or notable publication occurred by age 26. The Type G Automatic Loom was developed later in the 1920s.

name: Ingvar Kamprad
milestone_by_age_26: Founded IKEA as a mail-order trading company on July 28, 1943 at age 17, using a cash reward from his father for academic success, which he grew into the world's largest furniture retailer.
early_history_summary: Kamprad was born in Pjätteryd, Sweden, and grew up on the Elmtaryd farm (449 hectares, the largest in the area) in Småland. He began selling matches at age five, expanding to fish, Christmas decorations, seeds, and later pens and pencils. At age 17, while attending business high school in Gothenburg, he founded IKEA using a cash reward from his father for succeeding in his studies. The company was registered on July 28, 1943, initially selling pens, watches, and nylon stockings by mail order before adding furniture in 1948.
family_context_summary: Born on the Elmtaryd farm (449 hectares, the largest in the area) in Småland, Sweden. His paternal grandfather was from an aristocratic German family who purchased the estate. His grandmother encouraged his entrepreneurial endeavors and was his best customer. His father gave him a cash reward for succeeding in studies, which he used to found IKEA.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family ran a large farm; grandmother was an early customer and supporter of his selling ventures. Father provided cash reward for academic success. No specific retail or business domain expertise in the family, but the farm environment instilled frugality and resourcefulness.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early selling, family farm, frugality, self-taught business, mail order, Småland resourcefulness, direct customer exposure
evidence_summary: Kamprad began selling matches at age five and expanded to fish, decorations, and pens by his early teens, building over twelve years of selling experience before founding IKEA. At age 17, using a cash reward from his father for academic success, he registered IKEA as a mail-order trading company on July 28, 1943. He grew up on a large family farm in Småland, where frugality and resourcefulness were cultural values, and his grandmother was an early customer and supporter of his entrepreneurial ventures. He later diversified into furniture in 1948 and grew IKEA into the world's largest furniture seller by 2008.

name: Patrick Collison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Stripe (originally /dev/payments), a payment infrastructure company, with his brother John in 2010 at age 22, which grew into a company valued at tens of billions of dollars; previously co-founded and sold Auctomatic for $5 million in 2008 at age 19.
early_history_summary: Collison was born in Limerick, Ireland, to a microbiologist mother and electronic engineer father. He took his first computer course at age eight at the University of Limerick and began programming at ten. He won the BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition at age sixteen for creating Croma, a LISP-type programming language. He enrolled at MIT at age seventeen, co-founded Auctomatic with his brother John and Kulveer Taggar through Y Combinator, and sold it for $5 million within ten months. He dropped out of MIT and co-founded Stripe with John in 2010.
family_context_summary: Born in Limerick, Ireland, to a microbiologist mother (Lily) and electronic engineer father (Denis). Parents later became entrepreneurs, running a hotel and a corporate training company. Grew up in the small village of Dromineer, County Tipperary. Eldest of three boys.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents had scientific backgrounds: father in electrical engineering, mother in microbiology. This provided early exposure to science and technology. Parents also became entrepreneurs, providing a business-oriented household environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Young Scientist winner, MIT, Y Combinator, brother co-founder, scientific parents, early programming, Auctomatic exit, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: Collison, born to scientifically-trained parents in rural Ireland, began programming at age ten and won the BT Young Scientist competition at sixteen for creating a LISP-type programming language. He enrolled at MIT at seventeen and co-founded Auctomatic with his brother John through Y Combinator, selling it for $5 million within ten months at age 19. At age 22, he co-founded Stripe, which would become a dominant payment infrastructure company. His parents' scientific backgrounds, early access to computing at the University of Limerick, and the durable partnership with his brother John were critical enabling factors.

name: Sam Yagan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded SparkNotes, an online study guide company, during his senior year at Harvard in 1999 at age 22, and sold it for $30 million in 2000; later co-founded eDonkey (2002) and OkCupid (2003), all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Yagan was born in Chicago, the son of Syrian immigrants, and attended Harvard University as a math major. In 1999, during his senior year, he and his roommates Chris Coyne, Max Krohn, and Christian Rudder launched TheSpark.com (later SparkNotes), an online study guide. They sold it to iTurf for $30 million in 2000, when Yagan was 23. He then co-founded eDonkey, a P2P file-sharing network, in 2002, and OkCupid in 2003, all with the same Harvard peer team.
family_context_summary: Born in Chicago, the son of Syrian immigrants. His family valued education; he attended Harvard University as a math major. No significant financial resources documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being the son of Syrian immigrants.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Harvard, peer co-founders, math major, Syrian immigrant family, dot-com boom, SparkNotes, multi-venture team
evidence_summary: Yagan, the son of Syrian immigrants, co-founded SparkNotes during his senior year at Harvard in 1999 at age 22 with his roommates Chris Coyne, Max Krohn, and Christian Rudder. The company was sold for $30 million in 2000, making him a wealthy entrepreneur by age 23. He later co-founded eDonkey (2002) and OkCupid (2003), all with the same Harvard peer team. The dot-com boom and his Harvard network, particularly the durable team of co-founders from his freshman dorm, were critical enabling factors. His immigrant background provided motivation but no financial or network advantages.

name: Paul Dirac
milestone_by_age_26: Published the Dirac equation in January 1928 at age 25, unifying quantum mechanics and special relativity in one of the most important results in physics; also reformulated Heisenberg's matrix mechanics in November 1925 at age 23 and published the quantum theory of radiation in February 1927 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Dirac was born in Bristol, England, to a Swiss-French father who was a French teacher and a Cornish-English mother who was a librarian. He earned a BSc in electrical engineering from the University of Bristol in 1921 at age 19, then a BA in mathematics in 1923. He moved to Cambridge under Ralph Fowler and completed his PhD in June 1926 with the first thesis on quantum mechanics. He held an 1851 Research Fellowship from 1925 to 1928, during which he published his reformulation of Heisenberg's work (1925), the quantum theory of radiation (1927), and the Dirac equation (1928).
family_context_summary: Born in Bristol to a Swiss-French father who was a French teacher and a Cornish-English mother who was a librarian. The family was working-class; Dirac had a strained relationship with his strict, authoritarian father. His older brother died by suicide in March 1925.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a French teacher at Dirac's school; mother was a librarian at Bristol Central Library. No scientific or mathematical domain expertise in the family. Father's strictness forced the children to speak only French to him, which contributed to Dirac's famously taciturn nature.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught, engineering background, Cambridge, Fowler supervision, 1851 Fellowship, quantum mechanics wave, strict father, Bristol
evidence_summary: Dirac grew up in Bristol in a modest household with no family background in physics or mathematics. Despite this, he showed exceptional ability, earning two degrees from the University of Bristol by age 21. At Cambridge under Ralph Fowler, he quickly mastered the new quantum mechanics, publishing his reformulation of Heisenberg's work at age 23 and the Dirac equation at age 25 in January 1928. His engineering training gave him a distinctive approach to theoretical physics. He held an 1851 Research Fellowship from 1925 to 1928, which provided financial support during his most productive period. His father's strictness and the post-war economic depression that initially prevented him from affording Cambridge were formative constraints.
